traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements of story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are implemented and verified by automated tests and documentation:
- Core Functionality & REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION / REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA: The require-branch-annotation rule detects missing annotations on all specified significant branch types (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, and the major loop types). The valid/invalid tests in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts comprehensively cover these shapes, including default switch cases and various loop forms.
- Alternative Format Support & REQ-SUPPORTS-ALTERNATIVE: Multiple passing tests (e.g. “[REQ-SUPPORTS-ALTERNATIVE] if-statement with only @supports annotation is treated as fully annotated”, “try/catch where both branches are annotated only with @supports”, and “else-if branch with @supports inside the block body”) confirm that @supports is accepted as a complete alternative to separate @story/@req annotations.
- Comment Association & Annotation Parsing (REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): The rule and its helpers in src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts are exercised by tests that verify detection based on comments placed before branches, inline in switch cases, and inside catch/else-if blocks, including Prettier-reformatted code. The catch/else-if position and insert-position helper tests, plus the presence of valid/invalid cases with inline annotations, demonstrate correct association of comments to their corresponding branch nodes and parsing of @story/@req/@supports tags.
- Nested Handling & Integration (REQ-NESTED-HANDLING, Integration acceptance criterion): Tests explicitly cover nested if-statements with both annotated and missing inner branches, as well as complex try/catch and switch layouts, showing the rule behaves correctly in nested/complex control-flow structures. Additional helper and integration tests validate behavior under Prettier formatting and in realistic code scenarios.
- Configurability & Invalid Configuration Behavior (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE): tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts and the “[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE] …” tests in tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts confirm that: - branchTypes defaults to the expected set when unspecified, - branchTypes can restrict enforcement to specific branch node types, and - invalid branchTypes values are detected and reported as configuration errors, matching the story’s described invalid configuration behavior.
- Performance (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION and DoD performance item): tests/perf/require-branch-annotation-large-file.test.ts validates that the rule can analyze a large, deeply nested-branch file within a generous time budget, confirming that the implementation is efficient for files with many branches.
- Quality Standards & ESLint Best Practices: The rule is implemented as a standard ESLint rule module, with dedicated helpers and extensive RuleTester-based unit tests, plus performance and integration tests. Its integration into plugin presets is verified by tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts. The broader project uses modern ESLint and Jest setups and passes a large test suite, indicating adherence to ESLint rule development best practices.
- User Experience & Error Handling: The tests for invalid branch annotations (missing @story/@req, partially annotated branches, nested missing branches) verify that violations are correctly detected and reported. Additional tests for invalid configuration ensure clear configuration error reporting. While the exact text of user-facing messages is not repeated here, the focused tests around configuration errors and specific missing-annotation scenarios demonstrate that the rule provides precise feedback on which branches need annotations and why.
- Documentation: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md exists and, per prior detailed review, documents rule purpose, usage examples for all relevant branch types, configuration options (branchTypes), and invalid configuration behavior, matching the Documentation acceptance criterion and Definition of Done.
Given that the story text is unchanged from the previous assessment, all the same implementation artifacts are still present, and the full Jest test suite (including all branch-related rule, helper, configuration, and performance tests) passes successfully, this story is fully implemented and remains in a passing state.
